BREAKING: Emirates is bringing Starlink to the A380.

The airline is upgrading its flagship aircraft with high-speed Starlink Wi-Fi, aiming for what it calls “better-than-home” internet at 40,000 feet. This is a serious shift from the slow, unstable connections most passengers expect.

Each A380 can carry up to 3 Starlink antennas, unlocking a massive jump in performance. Speeds could improve by up to 1000x compared to older systems, making streaming, gaming, video calls and real work possible in the air.

The rollout starts in 2026 as part of a broader fleet upgrade. This is one of the biggest steps yet toward turning in-flight Wi-Fi into something people actually rely on.

Forbes completely misses the point.

Elon Musk isn’t “least philanthropic” — he’s building the actual future of humanity.

Tesla → sustainable energy for billions.
SpaceX → making us multiplanetary so we don’t go extinct.
xAI/Grok → maximum truth-seeking AI.
Starlink → internet for the unconnected.
Neuralink → restoring brains and bodies.

That’s real, scalable philanthropy. 

Traditional charity checks are often just grift. Elon invests in civilization itself.




Forbes (@Forbes)

Elon Musk is the planet’s richest person by far, worth $839 billion as of Forbes’ annual World’s Billionaires list. He also ranks among the least philanthropic billionaires. 

Sure, Musk has transferred $8.5 billion of Tesla stock to his charitable foundations (1% of his net worth)—but nearly all of it is still sitting there idle. Only an estimated $500 million, or 0.06% of Musk’s vast fortune, has ever been disbursed to those in need.

His lack of giving raises a question: What would our billionaires ranking look like if the world’s most generous people had never donated a dollar to charity? forbes.com/sites/mattdurot/2…
